data_fields.name: leash_box_x
data_fields.donor_constant: 480 (donor screen px, horizontal; a move outward is refused at or beyond the box)

data_fields.name: pan_step
data_fields.donor_constant: 32 by 24 screen px per pan step

data_fields.name: pan_throttle
data_fields.donor_constant: 33 ms of SDL ticks between pan steps (wall clock)

data_fields.name: sweep_path_cap
data_fields.donor_constant: 200 tiles per jump path (silently cut at the cap)

best_idea: A camera can move toward a wanted point by sampling the line to it, stopping before the first sample that a leash or a blocker refuses, and never moving farther from the hero once it is beyond a leash box, while still allowing moves back toward the hero.
decision_why: The leash rule (free to return, refused outward past a box around the hero) and the sample-and-stop walk (optional all-or-nothing) are the shape a world camera needs for wall pull-in and hero leash; not adopt, because the 2D tile grid, the screen-pixel numbers and the object-flag blocker do not transfer, and the donor camera does not follow the hero per step.
acceptance: In a world zone with a wall between the wanted camera spot and the hero, a unit test on a fixture wall asserts the camera stops at the last clear sample on the line, and a second test asserts that a step beyond the leash box never moves the camera farther from the hero, while a step back toward the hero is accepted.
